parsed.rationale: I don't agree that this ECG is normal: the QRS is wide (about 140 ms or more), there are broad, notched-looking monophasic R waves in I, aVL and V6, and V1–V3 show deep, wide QS/rS complexes with the ST segment and T wave pointing opposite the QRS (discordant), which fits left bundle branch block. The ST elevation in V1–V3 is small next to the deep S waves and points opposite the QRS, so it doesn't meet modified Sgarbossa criteria for STEMI.
